items.stem: Which is the definition of pressure?
items.answer: Normal force per unit area
items.markingKey: p = F/A with F perpendicular to the surface.

items.stem: Explain why snowshoes stop a person sinking into soft snow.
items.answer: They spread the person's weight over a larger area, reducing the pressure on the snow below the value at which it gives way.
items.markingKey: larger area [1]; smaller pressure for same weight [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the density of a gas is much lower than that of the same substance as a liquid.
items.answer: The molecules in a gas are much further apart, so the same mass occupies a much larger volume.
items.markingKey: molecules far apart [1]; larger volume for same mass [1] [2]

items.stem: A sample of oak is a cylinder of diameter 2.0 cm and length 5.0 cm with a mass of 11.8 g. Work out the density in kg m⁻³.
items.answer: 750 kg m⁻³
items.markingKey: V = 1.57 × 10⁻⁵ m³; ρ = 1.18 × 10⁻²/1.57 × 10⁻⁵ = 750 kg m⁻³. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A sample of brass (density 8500 kg m⁻³) is a cylinder of diameter 3.0 cm and length 8.0 cm. Calculate its volume and its mass.
items.markingKey: volume formula with lengths in m [1]; V = 5.65 × 10⁻⁵ m³ [1]; m = ρV = 0.481 kg [1] [3]

items.stem: A rectangular block of steel (density 7800 kg m⁻³) measures 0.10 m × 0.10 m × 0.50 m. (a) Calculate the minimum pressure it can exert on the floor. (b) Explain why the pressure depends on which face it rests on although the weight does not change.
items.answer: (a) 7650 Pa (b) p = F/A: the force is constant but the area of contact differs.
items.markingKey: (a) largest face (method/substitution) [1]; answer 7650 Pa with unit [1] [2] (b) p = F/A [1]; area changes [1] [2]

items.stem: Which is the definition of density?
items.answer: Mass per unit volume
items.markingKey: ρ = m/V.

items.stem: What is 1 g cm⁻³ in kg m⁻³?
items.answer: 1000 kg m⁻³
items.markingKey: 1 g cm⁻³ = 10⁻³ kg / 10⁻⁶ m³ = 10³ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: Describe how to determine the density of an irregular stone in the laboratory.
items.answer: Measure the mass on a balance; find the volume by displacement in a measuring cylinder (difference in readings); ρ = m/V; repeat and average.
items.markingKey: mass by balance [1]; volume by displacement [1]; ρ = m/V [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why a drawing pin has a broad head and a sharp point.
items.answer: The force is the same at both ends; the broad head gives low pressure on the thumb, the small point gives a very high pressure that pierces the board.
items.markingKey: same force both ends [1]; large area low pressure, small area high pressure [1] [2]

items.answer: 8500 kg m⁻³

items.stem: Estimate data: a camel standing on four feet; mass 600 kg, contact area 0.025 m² for each contact. Work out the pressure on the ground.
items.markingKey: p = mg/(nA) = 5890/(4 × 0.025) = 58 900 Pa. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A sample of concrete is a sphere of diameter 2.0 cm with a mass of 10.1 g. Determine the density in kg m⁻³.

items.stem: Estimate data: an elephant standing on four feet; mass 5000 kg, contact area 0.10 m² for each contact. Work out the pressure on the ground.
items.markingKey: p = mg/(nA) = 49 100/(4 × 0.10) = 1.23 × 10⁵ Pa. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: Compare the pressure exerted on the ground by a camel standing on four feet (mass 600 kg, contact area 0.025 m² for each of the 4 contacts) with atmospheric pressure (1.0 × 10⁵ Pa), and comment on the result.
items.answer: p = 58 900 Pa, which is 0.59 times atmospheric pressure.

items.answer: (a) 47.1 N (b) 9420 Pa (c) p = F/A: the force is constant but the area of contact differs.

items.stem: What is the pressure due to 10 m of water (density 1000 kg m⁻³)?
Derive the equation Δp = ρgΔh for a column of liquid.
items.answer: Consider a column of height Δh and base area A: volume AΔh, mass ρAΔh, weight ρAΔhg; pressure = weight/area = ρgΔh.
items.markingKey: mass = ρAΔh [1]; weight ÷ area = ρgΔh [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a dam is built much thicker at the bottom than at the top.
items.answer: Pressure in water increases with depth (Δp = ρgΔh), so the force on each square metre of the dam is largest at the bottom.
items.markingKey: pressure increases with depth [1]; larger force near base needs thicker wall [1] [2]

items.stem: A pressure sensor is lowered to a depth of 50 m in a tank of paraffin (density 800 kg m⁻³). Calculate the pressure due to the liquid alone.
items.markingKey: Δp = ρgh = 800 × 9.81 × 50 = 3.92 × 10⁵ Pa. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A diver swims 35 m below the surface of water (density 1000 kg m⁻³). Atmospheric pressure is 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa. Calculate the total pressure at this depth.
items.markingKey: Δp = ρgh = 3.43 × 10⁵ Pa [1]; add atmospheric [1]; = 4.44 × 10⁵ Pa [1] [3]

items.stem: An underwater camera housing is lowered to a depth of 8.0 m in sea water of density 1030 kg m⁻³; atmospheric pressure is 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa. (a) Calculate the pressure due to the water at this depth. (b) Show that Δp = ρgΔh by considering a column of water.
items.answer: (a) 80 800 Pa (b) weight of column ρAΔhg divided by area A gives ρgΔh
items.markingKey: (a) ρgh (method/substitution) [1]; answer 80 800 Pa with unit [1] [2] (b) mass of column [1]; divide by area [1] [2]

items.stem: The pressure at a point in a liquid at rest depends on …
options: the depth and the density of the liquid
the area of the container base
items.answer: the depth and the density of the liquid
items.markingKey: Δp = ρgΔh; it is independent of the shape of the container.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) A manometer contains water. The difference in levels is 12 cm. What is the pressure difference? (b) State the equation for the pressure difference between two points in a fluid.
items.answer: (a) 1.2 × 10³ Pa (b) Δp = ρgΔh

items.stem: Explain why the total pressure at the bottom of a swimming pool is not just ρgh.
items.answer: Atmospheric pressure acts on the surface and is transmitted through the water, so p = p_atm + ρgh.
items.markingKey: atmospheric pressure acts on surface [1]; added to ρgh [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why water in two connected tubes of different widths settles at the same height.
items.answer: Pressure at the same depth in a connected fluid at rest must be equal; pressure depends only on depth, not on tube width, so the surfaces are level.
items.markingKey: equal pressure at same level [1]; independent of width [1] [2]

items.stem: A diver measures the pressure due to the water above her. The density of the liquid is tripled while the depth stays the same. Predict, with a reason, how the pressure due to the liquid changes.
items.answer: The pressure due to the liquid triples.
items.markingKey: Using Δp = ρgΔh: pressure due to the liquid ∝ density of the liquid; factor = 3.00 = 3.00. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: Which statement is Archimedes' principle?
options: The upthrust equals the pressure at the bottom of the body
The upthrust equals the weight of the body
The upthrust on a body is equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces
The upthrust equals the mass of fluid displaced
items.answer: The upthrust on a body is equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces
items.markingKey: F = ρ_fluid g V_displaced.

items.stem: Use the idea of pressure to explain why a fully submerged block experiences an upthrust.
items.answer: The bottom face is deeper than the top face, so the pressure there is greater (Δp = ρgΔh); the upward force on the bottom exceeds the downward force on the top.
items.markingKey: pressure greater at bottom [1]; resultant upward force [1] [2]

items.stem: Show that the upthrust on a cuboid of height h and face area A submerged vertically in a fluid of density ρ is ρgV.
items.answer: Force difference = (p_bottom − p_top)A = ρghA = ρgV, since V = Ah.
items.markingKey: pressure difference ρgh [1]; × A = ρgV [1] [2]

items.stem: A steel block of volume 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ is fully immersed in oil (density 900 kg m⁻³), hanging from a newton meter. Calculate the upthrust on the block.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why the total pressure at the bottom of a swimming pool is not just ρgh. (b) Explain why water in two connected tubes of different widths settles at the same height.
items.answer: (a) Atmospheric pressure acts on the surface and is transmitted through the water, so p = p_atm + ρgh. (b) Pressure at the same depth in a connected fluid at rest must be equal; pressure depends only on depth, not on tube width, so the surfaces are level.
items.markingKey: (a) atmospheric pressure acts on surface [1]; added to ρgh [1] [2] (b) equal pressure at same level [1]; independent of width [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) State the equation for the upthrust on a body fully immersed in a fluid. (b) Which statement is Archimedes' principle?
items.answer: (a) F = ρgV, where ρ is the density of the fluid and V is the volume of the body. (b) The upthrust on a body is equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces
items.markingKey: (a) F = ρgV with ρ of fluid [1] (b) F = ρ_fluid g V_displaced.

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Use the idea of pressure to explain why a fully submerged block experiences an upthrust. (b) Explain why a helium balloon rises in air but a balloon filled with air does not.
items.answer: (a) The bottom face is deeper than the top face, so the pressure there is greater (Δp = ρgΔh); the upward force on the bottom exceeds the downward force on the top. (b) Upthrust = weight of air displaced; the helium balloon's total weight is less than this, giving a resultant upward force; the air balloon's weight (air + rubber) exceeds it.
items.markingKey: (a) pressure greater at bottom [1]; resultant upward force [1] [2] (b) upthrust = weight of displaced air [1]; comparison of weights [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why a helium balloon rises in air but a balloon filled with air does not. (b) Show that the upthrust on a cuboid of height h and face area A submerged vertically in a fluid of density ρ is ρgV.
items.answer: (a) Upthrust = weight of air displaced; the helium balloon's total weight is less than this, giving a resultant upward force; the air balloon's weight (air + rubber) exceeds it. (b) Force difference = (p_bottom − p_top)A = ρghA = ρgV, since V = Ah.
items.markingKey: (a) upthrust = weight of displaced air [1]; comparison of weights [1] [2] (b) pressure difference ρgh [1]; × A = ρgV [1] [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Describe how to determine the density of an irregular stone in the laboratory. (b) Explain why a drawing pin has a broad head and a sharp point.
items.answer: (a) Measure the mass on a balance; find the volume by displacement in a measuring cylinder (difference in readings); ρ = m/V; repeat and average. (b) The force is the same at both ends; the broad head gives low pressure on the thumb, the small point gives a very high pressure that pierces the board.
items.markingKey: (a) mass by balance [1]; volume by displacement [1]; ρ = m/V [1] [3] (b) same force both ends [1]; large area low pressure, small area high pressure [1] [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why the density of a gas is much lower than that of the same substance as a liquid. (b) Describe how to determine the density of an irregular stone in the laboratory.
items.answer: (a) The molecules in a gas are much further apart, so the same mass occupies a much larger volume. (b) Measure the mass on a balance; find the volume by displacement in a measuring cylinder (difference in readings); ρ = m/V; repeat and average.
